content.transcript: If you're on a GLP-1 and you haven't gone in three days, it's not your fault and it's not your diet. As a gastroenterologist, I see this on the shot every day. The bloating, the heaviness, the backed up feeling that won't quit. It's called a bile drought. Essentially, what's happening is the shot cut your appetite so hard that your body stopped releasing bile, the fluid that keeps your gut slick and moving. Without it, everything dries out, turns hard and gets stuck. And honestly, for a lot of women, it only gets worse the longer they stay on the shot. Now here's where most women go wrong. They grab more fiber and I get it. It's easy and it's what everyone tells you to do. But in a dried out gut, fiber just clumps into a hard plug and you end up more bloated and backed up than when you started. And Miralax, well, it forces water in to soften one block, but you dry right back out. And most women on a GLP-1 aren't looking to get hooked on something they have to keep taking just to go. Neither one fixes the real problem, the bile that stopped flowing. What I recommend instead is getting your bile flowing again. It's the fluid that keeps your gut slick. And once it's back, everything moves through on its own. Women tell me they're going regularly again within the first few days. And that's how quickly you can see a difference. Here's the catch. Your body makes bile when you eat, especially bitter greens, beets, and healthy fats. But on a GLP-1, you're barely eating, so nothing's telling your liver to release any. That's why I recommend Omyo. It takes those same bile-stimulating foods you can't eat enough of anymore and concentrates them into two capsules, so your liver starts releasing bile again, even when you're eating next to nothing. It uses concentrated bile herbs, milk thistle, artichoke, dandelion, and beet, to get your bile moving far better than fiber or water ever could, so your gut goes back to feeling slick, light, and finally regular. You just take two capsules a day. That's it. Women report no cramping, no urgency, no 1 a.m. sprints to the bathroom, and that they're going normally again within days. And by weeks 8 to 12, that's when they start to see the bloating settle down for good. Their gut feel calm again, and even the sulfur burps ease up. In fact, Omyo's results were so consistent that it's racked up over 2,500 five-star reviews from people on the shot. That's how well it works. So look, if you've been backed up and bloated ever since you started the shot, don't think fiber and Miralax are your only options. Thousands of women on the shot are already taking Omyo. Give it at least 60 days, and if you're not going regularly on your own, you get every penny back.
